newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - SOUTH KOREAN NEWSPAPERS - AUG 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - SOUTH KOREAN NEWSPAPERS - AUG 13.

text.p: The following is a summary of major stories in leading South Korean newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy.
- Remains of the victims who died in a fatal Korean Air Lines crash in Guam arrived in Seoul on Wednesday morning.

- Opposition leader Kim Dae-jung will meet with arch conservative Kim Jong-pil who heads the smaller opposition United Liberal Democrates to discuss unifying the opposition presidential candidate. Both leaders have been nominated as the torchbearers of their parties.

- In an effort to help ease the financial difficulties of subcontractors and parts suppliers to the Kia Group, the government Tuesday decided to expand its payment-gurantee limit to such firms to 500 million won from 200 million won.
- Korea has decided to take the United States to the World Trade Orgainzation (WTO) for bilateral consultation to resolve anti-dumping allegations against Korean semiconductor makers.

- Seoul's top Red Cross official said Tuesday that his organization will seek to establish a meeting point between separated family members of South and North Korea at the truce village of Panmunjom or any other site along the border.

- The Bank of Korea has extended $1 billion in emergency loans to seven commercial banks suffering from a serious shortage of foreign currencies in the wake of insolvencies or near bankruptcies of large business groups.
